Liam (customer): Hey team — after rotating our API key this morning, our backend started getting 401 invalid_api_key for every request. Nothing else changed in the app. Any quick checks?

Maya (support): Sorry you're seeing that, Liam. Can you paste the exact request you sent (no secrets if you want) or a redacted curl? Also which header are you using: `Authorization: Bearer <KEY>` or `x-api-key`?

Liam (customer): We're using `Authorization: Bearer <KEY>`. Here's a redacted curl we run from the container:```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX" https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/completions
```
The response is:```json
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{ "error": { "type": "invalid_api_key", "message": "The provided API key is invalid." }}
```

Ravi (sre): Quick thought: when you rotated, did you update the env var on the host/container? Also some folks accidentally copy a truncated key from terminals (last chars missing) or include a stray newline. Two quick checks: from the container run `echo -n $API_KEY | wc -c` to get length, and `printf "%s" "$API_KEY" | hexdump -C | head` to spot hidden chars.

Liam (customer): Running `echo -n $API_KEY | wc -c` returns `46`. Our docs show keys should be 48 chars. Hmm.

Maya (support): That looks like a truncated copy. When you rotated did you copy the key from the web UI? The UI shows a one-time only full key — if you close it early sometimes the last chars aren't selected on macOS double-clicks.

Liam (customer): Oh wow — we rotated and copied the key into our CI secret. CI log shows the secret was set, but I bet the copy missed the last two chars.

Andre (billing): FYI when a key is rotated we immediately revoke the old key for security. If the truncated key happened, you will definitely get 401s — that's expected.

Liam (customer): Recreated the secret with the full key, restarted the service, calls are green again. :tada: Verified `curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-<full>" https://api.redwood.example/v1` returns 200.

Maya (support): Glad that fixed it. A few followups we recommend: 1) Add a small script to validate key length on deploy (`[ $(echo -n "$API_KEY" | wc -c) -eq 48 ] || exit 1`), 2) Use our CLI `redwood keys list` to confirm active keys and fingerprints, 3) store the key in CI via paste as raw text, not by double-clicking in the browser.

Ravi (sre): Also added an automated check in deploy-bot to warn if API_KEY length != 48. I pushed that check to the staging pipeline. If anyone wants the snippet ping me. :gear:

deploy-bot: New pipeline check added: `check-api-key-length` — fail on mismatch.

Liam (customer): Thanks everyone — saved us an hour. Can we get this thread attached to our support ticket #23891 so it's searchable?

Maya (support): Done, linked notes to #23891 and included the `wc -c` tip. Closing this thread — reopen if you see any more 401s. :white_check_mark:

Andre (billing): Quick note for records: no requests reached billable endpoints while using truncated key, nothing to bill. Closing billing side.

Liam (customer): Appreciate it. Closing from our side too.
